subtitle: A turquoise cove in Curaçao's Bandabou district, named for the plantation where an enslaved man named Tula launched a revolt that grew to roughly 2,000 people in 1795.
spike_statement: Grote Knip beach takes its name from the Kenepa plantation, where Tula led Curaçao's largest slave revolt, roughly 2,000 people, on 17 August 1795.

levers.photo_tone: Turquoise cove walled by pale limestone bluffs, hard midday sun, coral-rubble sand, thatched palapas and rental loungers along the tree line
